# Database Schema

Concrete Postgres schema for the entities described in [`domain-model.md`](./domain-model.md),
implemented as SQLAlchemy models under `interview-practice.server/app/models/` (one file per
entity, all re-exported from `app/models/__init__.py`). The database URI is assembled in
`config.py` from the discrete `POSTGRES_*` variables in `.env` — see `deployment.md` for
why. See `api-design.md` for the Flask app factory + Blueprints structure this schema is
wired into.

**Primary keys are UUIDs**, generated by Postgres (`gen_random_uuid()`) on insert, not
sequential integers; every foreign key column is a `uuid` too. Schema changes go through
migrations — see [Migrations](#migrations) at the bottom.

This is a single-implicit-user prototype (see [ADR 0002](./adr/0002-single-user-prototype-no-auth.md))
— no `users` table exists yet; adding one later would mean adding an `owner_id` FK to
`documents` and `interviews`.

**Structured data gets columns or tables, not JSONB**, so the schema shows its shape
(see [ADR 0012](./adr/0012-document-analysis-cached-per-document-and-model.md)). There is
no JSONB column.

## `documents`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `type` | `enum(cv, cover_letter, job_description)` | |
| `name` | `text` | display name |
| `raw_text` | `text` | extracted content, what the LLM phases read |
| `source_filename` | `text` | original uploaded filename; always present, uploads are the only ingestion path |
| `file_path` | `text` | local-disk path, stored *relative to* the Flask app's `instance/` folder (e.g. `uploads/documents/<uuid>.pdf`), to the original uploaded file, so it can be downloaded back exactly as uploaded — same mechanism as `interviews.persona_image_path` |
| `saved` | `boolean` | `true` on upload for a CV or cover letter, `false` for a job description; changed by the candidate's "save for later" checkbox; a row always exists regardless (an Interview's FK needs something to point at), only `saved = true` rows are offered in the select-existing list |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |

## `document_analyses`

What phase 1 (JD/CV analysis) extracted from a `documents` row, cached so the document is
analyzed once and reused by every Interview that uses it. See
[ADR 0012](./adr/0012-document-analysis-cached-per-document-and-model.md).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `document_id` | `uuid`, FK → `documents.id` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, unique, not null | one-to-one: at most one analysis per document |
| `model` | `text` | OpenRouter model id that produced it; the cache key: an Interview whose `jd_analysis` model differs re-analyzes and overwrites the row |
| `domain` | `text`, nullable | the role's field (e.g. "backend engineering"); only for job descriptions and CVs |
| `company_name` | `text`, nullable | the employer, only read from job descriptions and cover letters; null when the document doesn't name one |
| `skills` | `text[]`, not null, default `{}` | concrete skills/tools, most important first; empty for cover letters |
| `likely_topics` | `text[]`, not null, default `{}` | subjects an interviewer would probe (for a CV: what its experience invites questions on); empty for cover letters |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now(); reset when the row is re-analyzed |

## `job_applications`

Groups multiple `interviews` rows as stages of the same real-world hiring pipeline. See
`domain-model.md`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `company_name` | `text`, nullable | null when the candidate gave none and none could be read from the job description / cover letter |
| `job_title` | `text` | |
| `seniority` | `text` | the candidate's level, taken from the Interview that creates the Application; it doesn't change between stages |
| `job_description_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `cv_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `cover_letter_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `progress_score` | `integer`, nullable | 1-5 aggregate rating of the overall level across the stages graded so far; same scale as the `interviewer_reviews.score_*` columns |
| `progress_summary` | `text`, nullable | narrative accompanying `progress_score`; both regenerated together once 2+ stages have an Evaluation — see domain-model.md |
| `progress_basis` | `text`, nullable | fingerprint (hash of the sorted `evaluations.id`s) of what the stored score and summary were built from; the pair is outdated when it no longer matches — see ADR 0015. Null while `progress_score` is |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |

Deleting a row here cascades (`ON DELETE CASCADE`) to every `interviews` row with this
`job_application_id`, and transitively to their `messages`/`evaluations`/
`interviewer_reviews` — see [ADR 0008](./adr/0008-jobapplication-delete-cascades-to-interviews.md).

## `interviews`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `job_application_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `job_applications.id` | nullable — a standalone Interview needs no Application |
| `job_title` | `text` | |
| `company_name` | `text`, nullable | the candidate's, else read from the job description / cover letter when either names one, else null; lets persona/conversation/ask-back suggestions reference a real company even when no JD is uploaded |
| `domain` | `text` | the field of the position: the documents' `document_analyses.domain` (job description, else cover letter, else CV) is only a hint, which phase 2 checks against `job_title` and company and drops when it doesn't fit (e.g. a software CV for a barista job), giving the job title's field instead; never entered by the candidate |
| `seniority` | `text` | |
| `difficulty` | `enum(easy, medium, hard)` | |
| `tone` | `text` | strict / neutral / friendly (a fixed set in the client form and the API's `Tone`); plain text rather than a DB enum so adding a tone needs no migration |
| `interview_type` | `text` | technical / behavioral (the API's `InterviewType`); plain text, same extensibility reasoning as `tone` |
| `interviewer_role` | `text` | recruiter / technical_screener / hr / hiring_manager (the API's `InterviewerRole`); plain text, same extensibility reasoning as `tone` |
| `target_question_count` | `integer` | soft cap, seeded by difficulty; 1–30 (`CHECK`) |
| `status` | `enum(in_progress, completed, abandoned)` | |
| `turn_started_at` | `timestamptz`, nullable | set while a Q&A turn is being processed so a second reply is refused (`409 TURN_IN_PROGRESS`); cleared when the turn commits or fails; ignored once older than 5 minutes — see ADR 0013 |
| `last_activity_at` | `timestamptz` | updated on every new message; staleness timeout 30 minutes — lazily detects a stale/ungracefully-closed session and marks it `abandoned` — see domain-model.md |
| `persona_name` | `text` | |
| `persona_title` | `text` | job title shown alongside `persona_name`; generated in the same phase 2 call |
| `persona_backstory` | `text` | the persona's background and knowledge scope, from the same phase 2 call; fed to the live conversation, never returned by the API |
| `persona_image_path` | `text`, nullable | local-disk path, relative to the Flask app's `instance/` folder; null until the portrait is generated (or if portrait generation is switched off) |
| `job_description_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `cv_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `cover_letter_document_id` | `uuid`, nullable, FK → `documents.id` | |
| `coaching_helpers_enabled` | `boolean` | set by candidate at creation; default `false` |
| `response_style` | `enum(concise, detailed)` | default `concise`; affects phase 3 phrasing and phase 5 write-up length |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |
| `ended_at` | `timestamptz`, nullable | |

## `interview_phase_settings`

Per-Interview LLM overrides for one phase (the "advanced settings" on Create Interview).
A row exists only for a phase the candidate overrode; no row means every setting of that
phase uses the global Preferences default.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | `uuid`, FK → `interviews.id` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, not null | |
| `phase` | `enum(jd_analysis, question_plan, live_conversation, coaching_helpers, evaluation, interviewer_review)` | |
| `model` | `text`, nullable | OpenRouter model id. `interviewer_review`'s choice is a narrower set (`google/gemini-2.5-flash`/`google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`/`gpt-5-mini`/`gpt-5-nano`/`typesafe/jev-1.13`) than the other 5 phases' — see architecture.md |
| `temperature` | `double precision`, nullable | |
| `max_tokens` | `integer`, nullable | |
| `reasoning_effort` | `text`, nullable | |

Unique: `(interview_id, phase)`. Any column left null falls back to the Preferences default.

## `preference_phase_settings`

The global Preferences: the default LLM settings of one phase, layered under an
Interview's own `interview_phase_settings`. The same columns, but not tied to an Interview.
A row exists only for a phase the developer customized, so no row means the built-in
default, and a row whose every setting is reset is deleted. Preferences is a singleton
with no table of its own: it is this set of rows (at most six).

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `phase` | `enum(jd_analysis, question_plan, live_conversation, coaching_helpers, evaluation, interviewer_review)`, unique | The same `generationphase` enum type as `interview_phase_settings.phase` |
| `model` | `text`, nullable | Limited to the same sets as `interview_phase_settings.model` |
| `temperature` | `double precision`, nullable | |
| `max_tokens` | `integer`, nullable | |
| `reasoning_effort` | `text`, nullable | |

## `interview_questions`

The question plan (phase 2): the ordered questions/topics the interviewer intends to
cover. Owned by the Interview and created with it; see `domain-model.md`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | `uuid`, FK → `interviews.id` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, not null | |
| `sequence` | `integer` | order within the plan, from 1; the first `target_question_count` are core questions, the rest reserves |
| `category` | `enum(technical, behavioral)` | |
| `question` | `text` | |

Unique: `(interview_id, sequence)`, which also serves ordered retrieval.

## `evaluation_criteria`

The Evaluation criteria (phase 2), one row per criterion; grounds the STAR evaluation
(phase 5). Never shown to the candidate.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | `uuid`, FK → `interviews.id` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, not null | |
| `sequence` | `integer` | order within the Interview's criteria, from 1 |
| `category` | `enum(technical, behavioral)` | same enum as `interview_questions.category` |
| `criterion` | `text` | e.g. "correctly reasons about time complexity tradeoffs" |

Unique: `(interview_id, sequence)`.

## `messages`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | FK → `interviews.id`, not null | |
| `phase` | `enum(qa, ask_back)` | |
| `role` | `enum(interviewer, candidate)` | |
| `content` | `text` | |
| `helper_text` | `text`, nullable | populated only for `interviewer`/`qa` rows when `interviews.coaching_helpers_enabled` is true |
| `is_clarification` | `boolean`, default false | an interviewer message that stays on the previous question; not counted as a question — see ADR 0013 |
| `sequence` | `integer` | ordering within the interview |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |

Index: `(interview_id, sequence)` for ordered transcript retrieval.

## `evaluations`

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | FK → `interviews.id`, unique, not null | one-to-one |
| `verdict` | `enum(hire, no_hire)` | |
| `reasoning` | `text` | |
| `strengths` | `text` | one strength per line; at least one |
| `weaknesses` | `text` | same, for weaknesses |
| `improvement_suggestions` | `text` | |
| `star_situation` | `text` | short assessment of the Situation, aggregated across the whole interview |
| `star_task` | `text` | same, for Task |
| `star_action` | `text` | same, for Action |
| `star_result` | `text` | same, for Result |
| `star_completeness` | `enum(strong, partial, weak)` | overall STAR completeness rating |
| `incomplete` | `boolean` | default false; true when interview was abandoned |
| `model_used` | `text` | OpenRouter model id the `evaluation` phase resolved to for this evaluation: the Interview's override, else Preferences, else the built-in `gpt-5-mini` (see architecture.md) |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |

## `interviewer_reviews`

Dev-facing "LLM-as-judge" assessment of the AI interviewer's own conduct, distinct from
`evaluations` (which grades the candidate). See `architecture.md`.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` PK, default `gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `interview_id` | FK → `interviews.id`, unique, not null | one-to-one |
| `judge_model` | `text` | OpenRouter model id used; default `google/gemini-2.5-flash` |
| `score_question_relevance` | `smallint` | 1-5 (`CHECK`) |
| `score_persona_consistency` | `smallint` | 1-5 (`CHECK`) |
| `score_pacing` | `smallint` | 1-5 (`CHECK`) |
| `reasoning` | `text` | |
| `created_at` | `timestamptz` | default now() |

## Relationships

- `documents.id` ← `job_applications.job_description_document_id` (nullable)
- `documents.id` ← `job_applications.cv_document_id` (nullable)
- `documents.id` ← `job_applications.cover_letter_document_id` (nullable)
- `job_applications.id` ← `interviews.job_application_id` (nullable — one application, many
  stage interviews)
- `documents.id` ← `interviews.job_description_document_id` (nullable, many interviews can
  reference the same saved job description)
- `documents.id` ← `interviews.cv_document_id` (nullable, same pattern)
- `documents.id` ← `interviews.cover_letter_document_id` (nullable, same pattern)
- `documents.id` ← `document_analyses.document_id` (one document, at most one analysis;
  deleting the document deletes it)
- `interviews.id` ← `messages.interview_id` (one interview, many messages)
- `interviews.id` ← `interview_phase_settings.interview_id` (one interview, at most one
  row per phase)
- `interviews.id` ← `interview_questions.interview_id` (one interview, many planned questions)
- `interviews.id` ← `evaluation_criteria.interview_id` (one interview, many criteria)
- `interviews.id` ← `evaluations.interview_id` (one interview, at most one evaluation)
- `interviews.id` ← `interviewer_reviews.interview_id` (one interview, at most one
  interviewer review)

## Foreign key behavior and indexes

- **`ON DELETE CASCADE`**: `interviews.job_application_id`, and `messages`/`evaluations`/
  `interviewer_reviews` `.interview_id` — deleting a `job_applications` row removes its
  interviews and everything under them (ADR 0008).
- **`ON DELETE SET NULL`**: every FK to `documents` (`job_applications` and `interviews`,
  each of `job_description_document_id`, `cv_document_id` and
  `cover_letter_document_id`). Deleting a Document leaves the
  interviews and applications that referenced it in place, just without the link. The
  columns are nullable already; blocking the delete instead was the alternative.
- **Indexes**: Postgres doesn't index foreign keys automatically, so the seven FK columns
  that aren't covered by another index are indexed (`interviews.job_application_id`, all
  three document FKs on `interviews`, all three on `job_applications`). `evaluations.interview_id` and
  `interviewer_reviews.interview_id` are covered by their unique constraint, and `messages`
  by the `(interview_id, sequence)` index.

## Migrations

Schema changes are versioned with **Flask-Migrate** (a Flask wrapper around Alembic). The
models in `app/models/` describe the *desired* schema; a migration is a script in
`interview-practice.server/migrations/versions/` that moves the *real* database there.
Writing or editing a model changes nothing in the database until you generate and apply a
migration. The migration files are committed to git; the database itself is not.

Run everything through `interview-practice.server/scripts/db.sh`, which loads `.env`,
checks the `POSTGRES_*` variables are set and Postgres is reachable, then calls
`flask db ...`:

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| Create a migration after changing a model | `scripts/db.sh migrate "add foo to documents"` |
| Apply all pending migrations | `scripts/db.sh upgrade` |
| Apply up to a specific revision | `scripts/db.sh upgrade <revision>` |
| Undo the latest migration | `scripts/db.sh downgrade` |
| Undo back to a specific revision | `scripts/db.sh downgrade <revision>` |
| Which revision is the database at? | `scripts/db.sh current` |
| List all migrations | `scripts/db.sh history` |

Postgres must be running and reachable at `POSTGRES_HOST:POSTGRES_PORT` — locally that's
`docker compose up -d db` (the Compose file publishes the port on `127.0.0.1` for this).

### Changing the schema

1. Edit or add the model. A new model file must also be imported in
   `app/models/__init__.py`, or Alembic won't see it and the migration comes out empty.
2. `scripts/db.sh migrate "short description"` — writes a new file in `migrations/versions/`
   and does **not** touch the database.
3. **Open and read the generated file.** Autogenerate is a draft: it can't detect column
   renames (it emits a drop plus an add, losing the data), and it handles changes to
   Postgres enum types poorly (adding a value to an existing enum needs a hand-written
   step).
4. `scripts/db.sh upgrade` to apply it.
5. Commit the migration file together with the model change.

### Rules of thumb

- **Never edit a migration that has been committed or shared.** Write a new one. A
  migration that exists only on your machine can be undone with `downgrade`, deleted, and
  regenerated after fixing the model.
- **Re-running is safe.** `upgrade` applies only what is missing — Alembic records the
  current revision in the `alembic_version` table — so running it on an up-to-date
  database does nothing.
- **`downgrade` can destroy data** (it runs each migration's `downgrade()`, which usually
  drops tables or columns). The script asks for confirmation when run from a terminal.
- **Starting over locally:** `docker compose down -v` deletes the `db-data` volume (and the
  uploads volume with it), then `docker compose up -d db` and `scripts/db.sh upgrade`
  rebuild an empty database.
- Migrations only run when you run them — nothing migrates on app start, and the app
  factory (`create_app()`) never touches the schema.
